Brake before the corner. Balance through it.

Carry speed through easy bends. For the longer rights, lift and briefly brake before turning. The car rotates as its rear tyres lose grip. Ease the steering, add throttle and countersteer to catch the slide. There is no drift button or automatic path-following. Fence contact is much slower than a clean, early brake.

Two complete stages

Choose the stage on the title screen. Savanna Sprint is a 3.23 km gravel course. Its starting clock is 47 seconds. The checkpoint adds 34 seconds. Pinefall Run is a 4.15 km mountain course. It starts on tarmac, changes to gravel at 1.30 km, and returns to tarmac at 3.24 km. The starting clock is 43 seconds. Its two checkpoints add 32 and 49 seconds. Brake before the right hairpin and use second gear. Cross the finish before the arcade clock reaches zero.

Arcade Rally has 14 rivals. The field is spread along the stage; the first car starts far ahead. Time Attack removes traffic and the time limit. Records and ghosts are separate for each stage, car, transmission, and physics engine. Replays use recorded car and rival positions. Use the replay slider and ½× / 1× / 2× controls. The results screen can start the other stage.

Use landscape orientation on phones. Recover re-centres the car and adds 3 seconds to your stage time; it subtracts the same amount from the arcade clock. The clock pauses when the tab loses focus. There is no reverse gear, damage meter, upgrade shop, loot or quest system.

About / completion report

DUSTLINE RALLY — TWIN STAGES
29 SEPTEMBER 2026 · GPT-6 ASTRA PRO · VERSION 3.0

Live Edition · visual update

Both complete stages are retained. This update adds visual feedback and moving scenery. It does not change the roads, race clocks, steering, tyre grip, or record keys.

Dust and tyre smoke now spread into soft trails. Rival cars raise dust. Collisions produce short spark trails. Gear changes at speed produce exhaust flames. Damp shoulder strips on Pinefall produce spray. Tyre marks remain for 22 seconds.

Animated clouds, waving spectators, birds, a broadcast helicopter, roadside grass, falling leaves, and moving river highlights give the stages more activity. The start gantry has countdown lights. Checkpoints and a successful finish release confetti. A slide-distance display and clean-pass notice give direct feedback without adding a score or bonus.

The shared audio manifest contains 37 original MP3 placeholders, including nine new ambient and effect sounds. No Sega recordings are included.

This file contains two complete, original rally stages inspired by Sega Rally Championship on Sega Saturn. It is not a ROM, port, extracted track, or verified copy of Sega's handling code.

Engine migration is not complete in the delivered file.The required npm archives could not be downloaded in the build environment. This file therefore runs the clearly labeled legacy renderer and custom physics. It does not embed Three.js or Rapier. The real Three.js and Rapier adapter code is included, together with a local archive importer. That adapter path was not run or checked against installed packages. It is not presented as a verified engine upgrade.

The new stage is playable without any package import. The 37 MP3 assets are original synthesized placeholders, not Sega recordings. Vite was not available; this file was compiled with TypeScript 5.8.3.

Launch

Save the HTML file. Open it in a browser that supports WebGPU or WebGL2. Use a full browser tab, not a file preview. No network or server is needed for the two-stage legacy build. Press a key or touch a control to unlock audio. Choose a stage, car, and transmission. Select Start Your Engine.

Keyboard: W / ↑ accelerates. A D / ← → steer. S / ↓ / Space brakes. Q / E shift in manual mode. C changes camera. R recovers the car with a three-second penalty. Esc / P pauses. F changes fullscreen mode. The How to Drive panel gives all gamepad and touch controls.

Local engine-package import

The Import Engine Pack button accepts the official three-0.186.0.tgz and rapier3d-compat-0.20.0.tgz npm archives. No installation or shell command is needed in the browser. The tool checks package names and exact versions, reads the module files, includes the licenses and any required WASM, and exports one new HTML file. Open that exported file to use the adapters. Importing packages does not change the running game's engine.

Package import does not prove that the untested adapter works on a device. Use official archives; the tool does not verify publisher signatures. No package download, external script request, or runtime network fetch is made by this file. A package or engine error stops startup instead of silently claiming a successful migration.

Source authority

The content reference is RGantela's Saturn Guide, version 0.50, 5 December 1995. Its Desert and Forest descriptions give the main turn sequences and scenery. The new course distances, widths, elevations, clocks, medals, and geometry are authored for this game. The guide is not treated as source code or a measured circuit map.

Systems and engine status

SystemImplementation
Playable stagesTwo distinct routes and environments. Stage selection and the results-screen stage link rebuild the scene and reset race state.
Input and menusKeyboard, standard gamepad, and multi-pointer touch controls. Title, controls, options, pause, results, and replay screens.
RecordsLocal best times and ghosts use separate keys for stage, car, transmission, and physics engine. Old Desert records remain readable on the legacy path. A blocked localStorage does not stop play.
Delivered rendererOriginal native WebGPU renderer with native WebGL2 fallback. Diagnostics explicitly say LEGACY. This is not Three.js.
Three.js adapterIncluded, inactive until the exact official package bytes are embedded. Uses WebGPURenderer, await renderer.init(), node materials, PCFShadowMap, an original floating-point HDR sky with PMREM, Timer, and optional TSL bloom through RenderPipeline. The automatic WebGL2 path keeps the same scene.
Rapier adapterIncluded, inactive until the exact package bytes are embedded. Rapier initializes before stage construction. A 1200 kg dynamic chassis receives engine, brake, and tyre impulses. Rapier integrates its position and resolves road, rail, rival, and debris contacts. Road mesh and guard colliders are simple. Active-body caps are 20 and 28. Stage replacement frees the physics world.
Fixed step and quality60 Hz simulation and interpolated car rendering. Auto measures frame time. Balanced and High change resolution, shadow size, effect cost, active-body limits, and update caps. Bloom is off by default and only runs on High.
Source-game audioNot supplied. The single audio manifest holds 37 original, embedded MP3 placeholders. Asset IDs let a future source or original sound pack replace them without editing game logic.
Build toolingThe delivered file was compiled with TypeScript 5.8.3. A pinned Vite build plan is embedded for migration, but Vite did not run here.

Additions

Pinefall Run has an original mountain layout, pine forest, lodges, gorge, guardrails, portal lamps, and finish area. Added systems include a stage selector, per-stage ghosts, two-checkpoint support, tarmac grip, stage-specific clocks and medals, new co-driver calls, and a link to the other stage. Both stages use original fictional cars and scenery. A local npm archive importer and single-file exporter are new maintenance tools.

Content outside these slices

The Mountain and Lakeside tracks, a full championship, multiplayer, licensed vehicle models, source music, and exact Saturn physics are not included. The source has no relevant quests, loot, equipment upgrades, or story inventory for these rally stages. No such systems are represented as unfinished features.

Known issues and test limits

The current Live Edition test record is below. The previous release also contained maintenance-tool tests. Those results do not verify the optional Three.js or Rapier adapter, and the archive importer was not retested for this visual update.

The requested libraries are absent from this delivered file. The adapter implementations were checked against current official API documentation and r186 source, but not against installed npm packages. Their runtime behavior is unverified. Native WebGPU, physical controllers, mobile performance, and direct file-URL launch require device tests. The managed test browser prevents file-URL navigation. The playable legacy build is not a substitute for the requested Three.js/Rapier verification.

The view from inside the tunnel has simple ambient light, not a full local-light solution. The river is decorative. Physics follows an arcade tyre model, not a detailed wheel-and-suspension simulation. Rivals follow authored race lines. There is no reverse gear. The field starts at intervals, so a stage win is not guaranteed. Fullscreen and storage depend on browser policy. Audio is synthesized, not sampled from Sega.

Hub migration notes

The engine interface separates graphics, physics, input, audio, quality, diagnostics, and loading from track and race logic. Replace the local package loader and engine/library-bridge.ts with the hub's central imports. The only library imports use bare specifiers. The optional bloom module is the official three/addons/tsl/display/BloomNode.js. It must also be supplied by the hub or built into the hub bundle.

The geometry adapter accepts linear vertex color, normal, roughness, metalness, and alpha data. It uses node materials instead of custom WebGL shader hooks. The legacy renderer still contains custom GLSL and WGSL. Remove that fallback once the official engine is tested and bundled. Namespace-based TypeScript can be converted to regular exports during hub integration. No custom class extends Three.js Object3D. Rapier owns body removal and world cleanup on the official path. No externally loaded assets or runtime CDNs are needed.

Version and API references

Three.js r186 release · RenderPipeline · WebGPU PMREM source · Rapier JavaScript World API · Rapier rigid-body API. The public r186 tag reported package version 0.186.1 during inspection. The importer therefore checks the npm package manifest for exactly 0.186.0; it does not assume that the tag proves the npm version. The Rust crate's June 2024 release notes were not used as JS release evidence.

Live Edition completion checklist

AdditionWhere and how it works
Surface trailsLoose surfaces produce dust. Tarmac produces tyre smoke during a slide or hard braking. Wet shoulder strips at 360–450 m, 980–1070 m, and 3520–3630 m on Pinefall produce spray. These strips are visual details; base tarmac grip does not change.
Driving feedbackShort impact sparks, exhaust flames on shifts above 12 m/s, a low landing puff on the Savanna crests, longer tyre marks, a live slide-distance counter, and clean-pass notices.
Race eventsThree start lights follow the countdown. Confetti is emitted once at each checkpoint and at a successful finish. Timeout results do not trigger finish confetti.
Living sceneryCloud banks and a sun disc on both stages. Spectators wave beside start and checkpoint areas. Birds and a tracking helicopter are visual objects. Forest leaves, roadside grass motion, low mist, and river glints add local movement. Extra forest light shafts can be enabled in Options. The new service tents, spare tyres, trees, and flags sit behind the starting grid.
Screen effectsSun glare is projected from the scene. Nearby canopy spheres and the Forest tunnel suppress it. Speed lines stay near screen edges. Brake lamps and sparks receive local glows. All HUD elements are rendered above these effects.
Controls and performanceVivid / Light / Off effect settings. Separate speed, glare, moving-scenery, and light-pulse controls. Reduced motion uses the browser preference as its initial value. High / Balanced and Auto remain available. New visual particles have caps of 230 / 115 in Vivid and 85 / 58 in Light on High / Balanced.

Visual update · source versus additions

These effects and live-scenery details are original additions. They are not presented as extracted Sega assets or exact source-game effects. The inherited Desert and Forest source checklists remain above. No further level, story, item, quest, vehicle, or handling system was added in this update.

Visual update · known issues and limits

The file still uses its explicitly labeled native legacy renderer and custom physics. The Three.js and Rapier adapter path is included but the official library bytes are absent. This visual update does not complete or verify that earlier migration.

Glare, light halos, and speed lines use a separate two-dimensional canvas above the 3D view and below the HUD. They are not ray-traced or volumetric lighting. Canopy-based sun occlusion is approximate. Transparent clouds, trails, and confetti use simple geometry; some intersecting transparent surfaces can show sorting artifacts. Particles do not add physics bodies or damage. The helicopter, birds, and crowds are scenery, not targets.

Visual particles are rebuilt during replay playback. A replay seek clears the old particles. Race positions are recorded; cosmetic particle positions are not. A car held on a rail will not produce a continuous flash: the original collision cooldown still applies.

Visual update · hub migration notes

engine/screen-fx.ts owns one disposable overlay canvas and cached glow sprites. It takes camera positions and effect cues through the engine interface. It uses no WebGL-only API and does not read the GPU buffer. game/race-effects.ts owns bounded cosmetic particles, world animation, and visual event hooks. The existing backend-neutral geometry builder supplies both renderer paths. No new library, copied dependency, custom shader, or runtime download was added.

The inherited native renderer and custom physics remain deviations from the requested hub stack. The unverified Three.js adapter and local engine-pack importer are unchanged in status. The renderer adapters receive matching new sun directions. On migration, validate the node-material alpha path, shadow bias, particle sorting, and optional scene bloom against the installed official packages. This HTML is compiled from TypeScript 5.8.3. Vite remains specified for the hub build but was not used to produce this standalone update.

Visual update · test record

The WebGL2 path passed three input-driven complete runs: Forest Arcade Rally in 1:48.35, Desert Arcade Rally in 1:17.65, and Forest Time Attack with manual gears and the hatch car in 1:46.60. Checkpoint bonuses, stationary timeout, replay scrubbing, stage changes, and separate in-session records passed. The effect pool stayed within its cap. A successful finish produced 90 confetti pieces on Vivid, even when dust had filled the pool. Light and Off settings, reduced motion, pause freeze, and the High/Balanced limits passed. Off cleared all overlay pixels. Keyboard input, simultaneous two-finger touch, and a simulated standard gamepad passed. All 37 MP3 files decoded and audio unlocked on input. No page errors or network requests occurred. Visual checks used desktop and phone-sized browser viewports with software WebGL2, not physical phones. Tests injected this HTML into a browser page because managed browser policy blocked file URLs. Native WebGPU, physical controllers, persistent local storage, direct-file launch, the optional library adapter, and target-device frame rate remain unverified.
